title: Rapid Variability of Sgr A* across the Electromagnetic Spectrum
question: Put the statistical properties of Sgr A*'s rapid variability across submillimeter, near-infrared, and X-ray wavelengths into the context of a single radiative model and determine the X-ray power spectral density.

evidence.quote: The NIR dataset used in this analysis is a combination of the extensive 2.12, 2.18, and 4.5 $\mu$m data of (cite: 2018ApJ...863...15W) and the 2.12 $\mu$m dataset of (cite: 2019ApJ...882L..27D).
We used 32 epochs (6641 minutes) of 345 GHz data from the LABOCA bolometer at the APEX telescope (cite: 2017A&A...601A..80S).

what.value: One epoch of 343 GHz SMA data

evidence.quote: We include one published (365 minutes—(cite: 2018ApJ...864...58F)) epoch of 343 GHz data and four new epochs (1573 minutes) of 230 GHz data from the Submillimeter Array (SMA).

what.value: 10 epochs of 70-minute ALMA light curves at 234 GHz

evidence.quote: The remaining 10 ALMA epochs are 70-minute light curves at 234 GHz (cite: 2020ApJ...892L..30I).

what.value: Intrinsic K-band flux density distribution and fraction of positive flux densities from VLTI/GRAVITY

evidence.quote: This value was derived from the most recent analysis of the intrinsic flux density distribution from the VLTI/GRAVITY interferometer ((cite: 2020A&A...638A...2G)).

what.value: Ratio of observed NIR flux densities at M and K bands R_obs = 12 +/- 0.5

evidence.quote: At an average (observed) flux density $S_{{K}} = 0.15$ mJy, (cite: 2018ApJ...863...15W) found the ratio of (observed) NIR flux densities at $M$ and $K$ bands to be $\Re_{\rm{obs}} = 12 \pm 0.5$.

recipe.goal: Extract submillimeter (ALMA, SMA, APEX) and X-ray (Chandra) light curves
recipe.method: Image ALMA data in 3-minute time bins with uniform weighting using task clean and measure peak flux densities and off-source RMS; vector-average SMA visibilities for baselines > 35-40 klambda; fit Gaussian point source in residual APEX maps; extract unbinned 2-8 keV Chandra photons within 1.25 arcsec aperture and barycenter-correct arrival times.
key_parameters: 3 minutes averaging time for ALMA light curves
1.25'' extraction radius and 2000-8000 eV energy range for Chandra
assumptions: Sgr A* is compact with flat visibility as a function of baseline length at mm wavelengths

recipe.goal: Cross-correlate simultaneous submm (230 GHz) and NIR (4.5 um) light curves
recipe.method: Compute discrete cross-correlation (DCC) function on raw and Hanning-smoothed logarithmic 4.5 um light curves with 230 GHz light curves using the Edelson & Krolik (1988) algorithm as implemented by Robertson et al. (2015).
key_parameters: Hanning smoothing kernel size of 61 minutes

recipe.goal: Determine the X-ray power spectral density (PSD) via Approximate Bayesian Computation (ABC)
recipe.method: Forward-model X-ray count-rate light curves from a broken power-law PSD and log-normal PDF with constant background, pileup correction, and 1-minute Poisson sampling; compare to observed Chandra first-order structure functions using weighted L2 norm distance in ABC.
key_parameters: 1-minute Poisson binning; pileup applied for count rates > 0.02 cps; structure function bin weights w_i = 1 (and w_i = 3 for the wide bin at large lags)
assumptions: Log-normal PDF for X-ray flux densities; broken power-law PSD with low-frequency slope gamma_0 = 0; effective area e_I = 1 for ACIS-S/HETG

recipe.goal: Fit single-zone synchrotron-SSC radiative model to submm, NIR, and X-ray variability
recipe.method: Simulate coupled slow and fast log-normal red-noise processes from shared Gaussian random numbers to drive optically thin synchrotron flux, cyclic magnetic field and source size evolution (injection, compression, expansion), self-absorption, cooling cutoff, and SSC X-ray emission; fit to eight structure functions, VLT K-band skewness and positive fraction, and M/K flux ratio via ABC.
key_parameters: 230 GHz structure function restricted to time lags < 50 minutes; VLT positive flux fraction target = 0.9; VLT skewness target = 3.44; M/K ratio R_obs = 12 +/- 0.5
assumptions: Single homogeneous spherical/slab synchrotron-SSC zone; R_S = 1.2e10 m; D_s = 2.523e20 m; A_K = 2.46 mag; A_M = 1.00 mag; X-ray extinction factor k_X = 3.39; slab-to-sphere volume factor 1.5 for electron density
Steady X-ray background equal for all three Chandra detector modes (chi_I = chi_G = chi_S)

score_reason: The authors publicly release the extracted light curves, the 5,000-particle ABC posterior chain, and the Python forward-modeling and visualization code (doi:10.17617/1.kctx3s25), and clearly write all model equations and priors. However, the C++/MPI ABC fitting code (which took ~10^6 CPU hours) is not released, and some low-level ALMA imaging/flagging parameters are omitted.
rediscovery_reason: Raw ALMA data are public in the archive, the extracted light curves and Python forward model are publicly archived with a DOI, and the main results (cross-correlation time lags, structure functions, and Bayesian model parameters) are quantitative.
